constructs.name: natural_recovery_propensity
constructs.description: Tendency for the original episode to remit or remain well without medication because of natural history, resilience, regression to the mean, and nonpharmacologic recovery.

constructs.name: past_escitalopram_response_tolerability
constructs.description: Historical symptom improvement, relapse prevention, side effects, and functional change while on escitalopram, reflecting drug effect plus natural recovery and expectancy.

constructs.name: patient_taper_preference_beliefs
constructs.description: Current motivation to taper or continue, perceived medication benefit, concerns about dependence or side effects, fear of relapse, and coping confidence.

constructs.name: taper_speed_dose_reduction
constructs.description: Rate and size of escitalopram dose reductions, including abrupt, linear, hyperbolic, paused, or reversed taper patterns.

constructs.name: adherence_to_regimen
constructs.description: Consistency with intended dose or taper plan, including missed doses, extra doses, and reinstatement behavior.

constructs.name: escitalopram_dose_taken
constructs.description: Actual escitalopram amount ingested at each model tick after taper instructions and adherence are realized.

constructs.name: duration_current_escitalopram_use
constructs.description: Length of continuous escitalopram use before taper decision, including time at stable maintenance dose.

constructs.name: stable_withdrawal_susceptibility
constructs.description: Stable person-specific susceptibility to SSRI discontinuation symptoms, distinct from the historical fact of prior withdrawal episodes.

constructs.name: neuroadaptation_dependence_state
constructs.description: Physiologic adaptation to sustained SSRI exposure that can make rapid reductions destabilizing even if the original disorder is inactive.

constructs.name: withdrawal_symptom_burden
constructs.description: Discontinuation symptoms after dose reduction, including dizziness, insomnia, anxiety, irritability, flu-like symptoms, nausea, and disequilibrium.

constructs.name: external_stressful_events
constructs.description: External shocks during follow-up such as loss, conflict, job strain, financial events, illness in others, or major schedule disruption.

constructs.name: perceived_stress_burden
constructs.description: Subjective stress load, threat appraisal, overload, uncontrollability, and daily hassles.

constructs.name: physical_activity
constructs.description: Amount and regularity of movement and exercise sufficient to affect sleep, reward, energy, and mood regulation.

constructs.name: sleep_circadian_disruption
constructs.description: Insomnia, hypersomnia, irregular sleep timing, circadian misalignment, and poor sleep quality.

constructs.name: clinical_monitoring_rescue_care
constructs.description: Frequency and quality of clinical follow-up, safety monitoring, medication review, dose rescue, and crisis support.

constructs.name: other_psychotropic_or_somatic_treatments
constructs.description: Concurrent medication changes, supplements, sleep aids, anxiolytics, stimulants, hormonal treatments, or somatic treatments affecting symptoms or exposure.

constructs.name: internalizing_symptom_burden
constructs.description: Primary outcome: latent depressive and anxiety symptom burden over the next two months, including mood, anhedonia, worry, irritability, somatic anxiety, and distress.

edges.description: Underlying remission and relapse propensity changes symptom burden independently of the taper pathway.
Natural improvement can be misattributed to escitalopram if medication began during spontaneous improvement.

sources.title: Posternak and Miller (2001). Untreated short-term course of major depression.
sources.snippet: Wait-list studies show measurable spontaneous improvement over weeks.

edges.description: Perceived benefit and acceptable tolerability make extended use more likely.
Perceived past benefit discourages tapering, while side effects or lack of perceived benefit encourage it.
Worsening symptoms can increase fear of tapering; wellness can increase confidence to taper.
Motivation, fear of relapse, and coping confidence affect how quickly the person attempts to reduce dose.
Beliefs about benefit, harm, or dependence influence missed doses, self-directed dose changes, and reinstatement.
Planned reductions mechanically lower the subsequent amount of escitalopram taken.
Missed doses, extra doses, and partial adherence change actual escitalopram dose relative to the plan.

sources.title: DiMatteo, Lepper, and Croghan (2000). Depression is a risk factor for noncompliance with medical treatment.
sources.snippet: Depression is associated with poorer adherence to medical regimens.

edges.description: Worsening depression or anxiety can reduce organization and motivation for taking medication as intended, or prompt rescue dosing.

sources.title: DiMatteo, Lepper, and Croghan (2000). Depression is a risk factor for noncompliance with medical treatment.
sources.snippet: Depressed patients were less likely to adhere to treatment recommendations.

edges.description: Withdrawal symptoms can lead to pausing the taper, reinstating, or taking rescue doses.

sources.title: Horowitz and Taylor (2019). Tapering of SSRI treatment to mitigate withdrawal symptoms.
sources.snippet: Withdrawal symptoms can motivate reinstatement and slower tapering.

edges.description: Discontinuation symptoms update beliefs about how risky or feasible tapering is.
Longer continuous exposure allows more physiologic adaptation to SSRI blockade.

sources.title: Horowitz and Taylor (2019). Tapering of SSRI treatment to mitigate withdrawal symptoms.
sources.snippet: Withdrawal risk is framed in relation to adaptation and nonlinear dose occupancy.

edges.description: Underlying discontinuation susceptibility causally affects current withdrawal burden, while prior history is treated as a marker and belief-shaper.

sources.title: Davies and Read (2019). A systematic review into antidepressant withdrawal effects.
sources.snippet: Withdrawal reactions are variable in incidence, duration, and severity.

edges.description: Faster or larger dose reductions can precipitate withdrawal when physiologic adaptation and susceptibility are present.
Greater adaptation to chronic SSRI exposure increases susceptibility to symptoms when exposure falls.

sources.title: Davies and Read (2019). A systematic review into antidepressant withdrawal effects.
sources.snippet: Withdrawal reactions are reported by a substantial proportion of discontinuers.

edges.description: Discontinuation symptoms often include insomnia or disturbed sleep, which can worsen mood and anxiety.

sources.title: Davies and Read (2019). A systematic review into antidepressant withdrawal effects.
sources.snippet: Insomnia and related symptoms are among reported withdrawal effects.

edges.description: Unpleasant or frightening withdrawal sensations increase threat appraisal and stress.
Withdrawal can directly raise anxiety, irritability, low mood, distress, and somatic symptoms.

sources.title: Lewis et al. (2021). Maintenance or Discontinuation of Antidepressants in Primary Care.
sources.snippet: Discontinuation increased relapse and withdrawal symptoms compared with maintenance.

edges.description: Actual dose changes the maintenance of antidepressant benefit and can alter subsequent internalizing symptom burden.
External life events and demands increase perceived stress depending on appraisal and resources.

sources.title: Hammen (2005). Stress and depression.
sources.snippet: Stressful experiences are central precipitants and maintainers of depression.

edges.description: Stress and arousal impair sleep onset, continuity, and circadian regularity.
Perceived overload and threat directly increase anxiety, dysphoria, irritability, and bodily arousal.
Regular physical activity improves sleep pressure, circadian stability, and sleep quality.
Exercise can directly improve mood, anxiety, energy, and self-efficacy.

sources.title: Schuch et al. (2016). Exercise as a treatment for depression.
sources.snippet: Physical exercise was associated with reduced depressive symptoms.

edges.description: Poor sleep and circadian disruption worsen next-period mood, anxiety, irritability, energy, and concentration.

sources.title: Baglioni et al. (2011). Insomnia as a predictor of depression: a meta-analytic evaluation of longitudinal epidemiological studies.

edges.description: Depression and anxiety can disturb sleep through worry, arousal, hypersomnia, irregular routines, and low activity.
Symptoms reduce energy, motivation, confidence, and routine, lowering subsequent physical activity.
Severe discontinuation symptoms prompt clinician contact and potential taper modification.
Worsening symptoms prompt more clinical contact, safety monitoring, and treatment adjustment.
Clinical contact can initiate or change adjunctive treatments for sleep, anxiety, mood, or medical contributors.
Other medication or somatic treatment changes can improve or worsen mood and anxiety independently of escitalopram tapering.
